title: Cell surface profiling of cultured cells by direct hydrazide capture of oxidized glycoproteins
author: Tremblay, Fauteux, et al.

steps.title: Prepare oxidation and quenching solutions
steps.instruction: Make fresh solutions on ice and keep covered with foil: oxidation solution – dissolve 0.086 g sodium meta‑periodate (NaIO₄) in a 50 mL conical tube, cover with aluminum foil and add 40 mL cold PBS pH 6.5 to give 10 mM NaIO₄; quenching solution – dissolve 0.252 g sodium sulfite (Na₂SO₃) in a 15 mL conical tube and add 10 mL cold PBS pH 6.5 to give 200 mM Na₂SO₃ (10×). Keep both solutions on crushed ice.

steps.title: Grow cells to appropriate confluency
steps.instruction: Culture the desired adherent cells to ~80 % confluence (≈20–30 million cells, typically using two 150 mm plates to obtain >1 mg total protein).

steps.title: Place cells on ice before oxidation
steps.instruction: For adherent cells, place the culture plates on a flat bed of crushed ice; for suspension cells, pellet 50 mL of culture at 200 g for 5 min at 4 °C and keep the tube on ice.

steps.title: Oxidize cell‑surface glycans
steps.instruction: Remove culture media and slowly add 18 mL cold oxidation solution to each plate (or tube). Cover with foil and incubate on ice for 10 min, rocking plates every 2 min to prevent drying (tubes need not be rocked).

steps.title: Quench the oxidation reaction
steps.instruction: Add 1900 µL cold 10× quenching solution to each plate (final ≈20 mM Na₂SO₃). Mix gently by rocking, then incubate on ice for an additional 6 min, rocking plates every 2 min.

steps.title: Harvest cells after oxidation
steps.instruction: For adherent plates: transfer 8 mL of the oxidation mixture to a 50 mL tube on ice, scrape remaining cells with a cell scraper, add 5 mL cold PBS pH 6.5, swirl, and combine all into the same tube. For suspension cells, skip to the next step.

steps.title: Pellet cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 g for 5 min at 4 °C and carefully discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend cell pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL cold PBS pH 6.5, transfer to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge again at 400 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard PBS, and proceed directly to lysis or freeze at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare coupling and lysis buffers
steps.instruction: Hydrazide coupling buffer (100 mM NaOAc, 150 mM NaCl, pH 5.5): dissolve 6.8 g sodium acetate trihydrate and 4.4 g NaCl in 450 mL water, adjust pH to 5.5 with acetic acid, bring volume to 500 mL, filter (0.22 µm) and store at RT. Lysis buffer: add 0.025 g SDS to 5 mL coupling buffer (0.5 % SDS final), keep on ice; immediately before use add protease inhibitor cocktail (1/200) and benzonase (1/1000).

steps.title: Lyse cells and clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Add 1–5 mL lysis buffer to the cell pellet (≈10 × pellet volume, e.g., 2 mL for a 200 µL pellet). Homogenize by passing the suspension through a 3 mL syringe with a 33 G needle 5 times. Rotate at RT for 30 min–2 h until the sample is no longer viscous (DNA degraded). Centrifuge 10 min at RT, 4500 g; transfer the cleared supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Quantify and adjust protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure protein using a Detergent‑Compatible (DC) assay (Bio‑Rad). Dilute the lysate with additional lysis buffer to obtain 1–1.3 mg mL⁻¹ protein. Aliquot and freeze at –80 °C or proceed to hydrazide capture.

steps.title: Prepare Affi‑Gel Hz beads
steps.instruction: Cut the tip off a 1000 µL pipette tip to widen the opening. Transfer bead suspension to a 1.5 mL tube so that 50 µL settled beads are available per mg of protein (add a slight excess). Centrifuge 100 g for 1 min, discard supernatant, and wash beads 4× with 1 mL hydrazide coupling buffer (flick and invert; never vortex). After the final wash, add 1 mL coupling buffer and let beads settle by gravity. Aliquot the washed beads for each sample.

steps.title: Capture oxidized glycoproteins on beads
steps.instruction: Using a 200 µL gel‑loading tip, remove most of the wash buffer from each bead tube. Add the oxidized cell lysate (typically 1 mg protein; 0.5–2 mg acceptable) to the semi‑dry beads, resuspend gently by flicking/inverting, and incubate on a rotator at RT overnight (12–18 h).

steps.title: Wash beads and remove unbound proteins
steps.instruction: Label a mini‑spin column and place it in a 2 mL tube. Centrifuge the bead suspension at 100 g for 1 min, discard supernatant, and add 500 µL Urea Buffer (8 M urea, 0.4 M ammonium bicarbonate). Resuspend beads, transfer to the mini‑spin column, and wash 8 times with 500 µL Urea Buffer followed by 4 times with 500 µL 50 mM AMBIC (use a vacuum manifold or centrifuge at 100 g for 15 s each wash).

steps.title: Reduce and alkylate bead‑bound proteins
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 10 mM DTT to the beads, cap, and incubate at 56 °C for 1 h. Spin 100 g for 15 s, discard supernatant. Add 500 µL 25 mM iodoacetamide (IAA), cap, invert, and incubate at RT for 1 h in the dark. Spin 100 g for 15 s, discard supernatant, then wash beads 4 times with 500 µL Trypsin Digest Solution (50 mM AMBIC + 15 % ACN) if using trypsin, or 4 times with 500 µL 50 mM AMBIC if using chymotrypsin.

steps.title: Protease digestion of captured glycoproteins
steps.instruction: Add sequencing‑grade trypsin at 1 % (w/w) (e.g., 10 µg trypsin per 1 mg lysate) in 500 µL Digest Solution (or chymotrypsin at the same ratio in 500 µL 50 mM AMBIC). Cap, seal with parafilm, invert to mix, place the tube on a head‑over‑head rotator, and incubate O/N: 37 °C for trypsin or 25 °C for chymotrypsin. After digestion, centrifuge 100 g for 15 s to collect the flow‑through (optional). Then wash beads sequentially: 3 × 500 µL 1.5 M NaCl, 3 × 500 µL organic wash (60 % ACN, 0.1 % TFA), 3 × 500 µL MeOH, and finally 6 × 500 µL 50 mM AMBIC to remove all non‑glycosylated peptides and solvents.

steps.title: Release N‑linked glycopeptides with PNGase F
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 50 mM AMBIC to the beads, spin 1 min at 1500 g, and carefully remove the supernatant. Add 100 µL 50 mM AMBIC containing 4 U PNGase F (per 1 mg lysate) to the beads, flick to resuspend, and incubate O/N (12–18 h) at 37 °C without shaking. Transfer the supernatant to a new tube, add another 100 µL 50 mM AMBIC, mix, let beads settle, and pool the supernatant. Repeat the 100 µL addition once more and pool all supernatants.

steps.title: Desalt and concentrate released peptides
steps.instruction: Pre‑wet a fresh mini‑spin column with 400 µL 50 mM AMBIC (centrifuge 100 g for 1 min in a 2 mL tube). Spin the pooled peptide solution through the column at 100 g for 1 min to remove any residual beads. Concentrate the flow‑through in a speed‑vac to a final volume of ~30–60 µL, then store at –80 °C until mass‑spectrometry analysis.
